title: Cooking ratios
summary: The fixed proportions by weight underneath a recipe: 1:1 roux, 3:1 vinaigrette, a 5 percent brine. They scale where a cup measure does not.

explain: states at least three working ratios by weight and what each one produces
apply: scales a 3:1 vinaigrette to four times the volume without tasting it flat

title: Heat control
summary: Matching the energy under the pan to what the food needs, steered by sound, colour and smell rather than a number on a dial.

explain: distinguishes conduction, convection and radiation and gives one pan example of each
apply: preheats a heavy pan for a sear and lets it recover between batches

title: Emulsions
summary: Fat held as droplets in water, or the reverse, kept apart by an emulsifier such as mustard, egg yolk lecithin or the proteins in butter.

misconceptions.text: Once an emulsion holds, it is stable and can be boiled.

explain: names the dispersed fat, the continuous water phase and the emulsifier
apply: mounts a pan sauce with cold butter off the heat and keeps it glossy
discriminate: separates a sauce held by emulsion from one thickened by reduction

title: Reduction
summary: Boiling water out of a liquid to concentrate flavour, gelatin and body, which concentrates salt and acid at the same rate.

explain: explains that a reduction concentrates salt and acid along with the flavour
discriminate: separates body that came from gelatin from body that came from butter

title: Deglazing
summary: Lifting the browned fond off the pan with a liquid, so the flavour that stuck to the metal ends up in the sauce.

explain: says what the fond is and why water alone lifts it
apply: deglazes a hot pan without dropping the temperature so far that the sauce stalls

title: Pan sauces
summary: The sauce built in the pan the protein just left: fond, a deglazing liquid, a reduction and butter mounted off the heat.

explain: gives the four steps in order and says what each one is for
apply: sends a pan sauce that is still glossy ten minutes after it was made
